title: E8 checking-order checkpoint form B
instructions: Composition checkpoint. The prompt asks how something you learned at school helped solve an everyday problem and what you learned. Your notes: in mathematics you learned to compare unit prices rather than package prices; at home you compared two rice packages using their labelled price per kilogram; one was cheaper per kilogram although its package price was higher; your family chose it because the amount suited the meals you had planned; you learned to compare like quantities while still thinking about what you actually need. You have eight minutes left to check your composition. You notice that one sentence says your choice is best for every family, that your first sentence describes the music playing in the supermarket, and that two sentences are joined only by a comma. Make all five decisions.

parts.prompt: Which check should you do first?

options.text: Fix the two sentences joined only by a comma.
Remove the claim that your choice is best for every family.
Change a word that appears twice in one paragraph.
Shorten one sentence in your final paragraph.

choice_rationales.A: Punctuation belongs in the final sentence check.
choice_rationales.B: The claim is not supported by your notes, so the content must be fixed first.
choice_rationales.C: Repeated words are a small style point.
choice_rationales.D: Sentence length is polish, not a problem with the content.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Accurate content and the task come before surface checks.

parts.prompt: Which order of paragraphs gives the reader the clearest logic?

options.text: Home need → school comparison idea → unit-price comparison → choice and its limit → what I learned
Choice → supermarket music → school idea → a new topic that appears only in the conclusion
What I learned → package colours → choice → invented figure
Comma check → choice → unrelated memory

choice_rationales.A: It explains the basis for the decision before reporting it.
choice_rationales.B: The music and the new topic break the logic.
choice_rationales.C: Unrelated details and an invented figure confuse the reader.
choice_rationales.D: A punctuation check is not a paragraph, and the memory is irrelevant.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A clear response explains the basis for the decision before reporting it.

options.text: I compared the labelled price per kilogram on both packages.
The lower unit price belonged to the package with the higher total price.
A cheerful song was playing through the supermarket speakers.
We also checked that the amount matched the meals we planned.

choice_rationales.C: The music does nothing to answer the prompt.
choice_rationales.D: This explains why the family chose that package.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A detail with no job in the response should be removed.

parts.prompt: Which sentence about what you learned is best supported?

options.text: The largest package is always the right choice because it gives the most rice.
Comparing like quantities helps a decision, but the amount must still match what you actually need.
All families should buy exactly the same rice as we did.
The price on the package never matters at all.

choice_rationales.A: One comparison cannot prove a rule for every purchase.
choice_rationales.B: It uses the mathematical idea without turning it into a rule for everyone.
choice_rationales.C: Families have different needs, and the notes do not support this.
choice_rationales.D: This is an absolute claim the notes do not support.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The lesson applies the school idea without turning it into an absolute rule.

parts.prompt: Which check belongs in your last pass?

options.text: Make sure that two complete sentences are not joined only by a comma.
Put back the claim that your choice is best for every family.
Move the final choice so that it comes before the price comparison.
Add a savings percentage that you did not work out.

choice_rationales.A: Sentence boundaries are a final-pass check that does not change the meaning.
choice_rationales.B: This would make the content inaccurate again.
choice_rationales.C: This would undo the order you fixed.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The final pass checks sentence boundaries without changing the meaning.
